title: Microsoft Dataverse: bulk delete gains run details and solution-aware jobs
notes: claim 50: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The roadmap facts, admin paths and solution-import warnings are supported. The bulk-delete API instructions omit required request parameters, so they are not sufficient to submit the documented request. The assertion that end users never see the changes also goes beyond the documentation.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Bulk delete jobs are solution aware and can move between environments in solutions.
claims.quote: Bulk delete jobs are solution-aware, so you can add them to a solution to make them portable across environments.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Bulk deletion is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Data management > Bulk deletion.
claims.quote: select Manage ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Data management, then select Bulk deletion.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first API row
claims.claim: The printed BulkDelete POST instructions specify a request body containing QuerySet, JobName and StartDateTime.
claims.quote: SendEmailNotification | Edm.Boolean | False; ToRecipients | Collection(activityparty) | False; CCRecipients | Collection(activityparty) | False; RecurrencePattern | Edm.String | False
claims.fix: Replace the call in both locations with 'POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/BulkDelete with JSON body {"QuerySet": <query-expression array>, "JobName": "<job name>", "SendEmailNotification": false, "ToRecipients": [], "CCRecipients": [], "RecurrencePattern": "", "StartDateTime": "<ISO 8601 start time>"}'. The existing cited developer article shows these fields together; the action reference at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/bulkdelete confirms that the four omitted parameters are non-nullable.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A job that fails or ends prematurely does not roll back records already deleted.
claims.quote: If a bulk delete job fails or ends prematurely, the operation doesn't roll back any deleted records. The record data remains deleted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Selecting the wizard's Permanent deletion checkbox permanently removes records so they cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: The Bulk Deletion Wizard includes a Permanent deletion checkbox. When selected, records deleted by the bulk delete job are permanently removed and can't be recovered.

claims.where: Governance controls: closing paragraph
claims.claim: Permanent deletion is a per-job option that skips deleted-record tables when deleted record keeping is enabled.
claims.quote: If deleted record keeping is turned on for your environment, this option skips the step of moving data to deleted records tables, which results in faster job execution.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.quote: Delete data periodically. ... Schedule the start time of a recurring bulk delete.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Bulk deletion can trigger a table's delete plug-ins or workflows for each deleted record.
claims.quote: If the delete action on a specific table type triggers a plug-in or a workflow (process), the bulk delete job triggers the plug-in or workflow every time it deletes a table record of that type.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Bulk deletion removes unneeded data at scale to manage system storage consumption.
claims.quote: The bulk deletion feature helps you delete data you no longer need so you can maintain data quality and manage the consumption of system storage.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated how existing, unpackaged bulk deletion jobs are affected by these improvements.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse bulk delete solution aware existing unpackaged jobs changes. Read Learn delete-bulk-records and delete-data-bulk and search excerpts for asynchronous-service and cleanup-asyncoperationbase-table; no migration effect on unpackaged jobs was stated.

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: Learn does not describe a separate prerequisite or enablement flag for the Run details tab.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse bulk delete Run details enable prerequisites feature setting flag. Read Learn delete-bulk-records and delete-data-bulk plus governance-policy prerequisites excerpt; no separate Run details prerequisite or flag was documented.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's example tests a bulk deletion job in a sandbox, validates it in preproduction and then imports its solution into production.
claims.quote: For example, develop and test a bulk deletion job in a sandbox environment, validate it in preproduction, then import the solution into production.

claims.where: rationale: impact
claims.claim: End users do not see these changes.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse bulk delete Run details solution aware end users administrators visibility. Read delete-bulk-records and delete-data-bulk; they document administrative surfaces and privileges, but do not state that end users cannot see the changes.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with 'Low. The documented changes appear in bulk deletion settings and the solution explorer, so this briefing expects administrators and solution owners to notice them.' Keep the low impact rating as the wiki's judgement.
